children.title: Ethics-Based Auditing as a Governance Mechanism for Automated Systems

detail.title: Ethics-Based Auditing as a Governance Mechanism for Automated Systems
detail.summary: Ethics-based auditing (EBA) provides a formal, though 'soft', governance framework for automated decision systems. While autonomy is complex, EBA helps bridge the gap between automated outputs and decision-subject justifications by mandating consistent documentation and ethical deliberation at key intervention points.
detail.reason: Revision incorporating new evidentiary support for governance and autonomy.

detail.title: Architectural Distinctions in Preference Formation
detail.summary: Long-term preference formation in autonomous agents is not solely a function of internal state adaptation but is constrained by hierarchical autonomy (global vs. local), explicit ethics-based auditing frameworks, and physical control constraints that dictate resilience. These structural layers separate transient behavioral responses from persistent decision-making preferences.
detail.reason: Incorporating findings on governance (EBA) and control constraints (CAV controllability) to refine the distinction between transient behavior and preference formation.

detail.title: Architectural Distinctions in Preference Formation
detail.summary: This revision applies quantitative methods to the study of preference formation, arguing that distinguishing transient behavioral states from long-term preferences requires empirical validation frameworks. While global autonomy provides a governance structure, local behavioral adaptations—often misidentified as persistent preferences—must be statistically verified as patterns rather than noise.
detail.reason: Revision incorporating empirical methodology as a requirement for preference stability analysis.

children.title: Emergence of Responsibility and Accountability in Autonomous Agents

detail.title: Emergence of Responsibility and Accountability in Autonomous Agents
detail.summary: Responsibility in autonomous agents is operationalized not through internal intent, but through auditable constraint frameworks. Resilience in control systems depends on treating communication and interaction quality as active control constraints rather than implicit assumptions, bridging the gap between engineering behavior and ethical accountability.
detail.reason: Incorporating resilience and control constraints into the governance model for responsibility.
